title: Llama API Pricing: Per-Token Rates and Limits (2026)
summary: Llama API pricing differs across models and usage tiers. Compare rates for different Llama options to estimate costs for your workload.
body_markdown:
## Account for hidden Llama API costs and limits


Three things never show up in the headline per-million-token rate: the rate limits that throttle you, the tokens you pay for twice, and price changes that arrive without your asking. Budget for all three.


Treat "unverified" items as questions to put to Meta, not as facts; the list below sorts each risk by whether Meta's documentation backs it.


- Rate limits of 10 requests per minute and 250,000 tokens per minute in preview: in docs
- Waitlist access to the API: unverified
- Retries billed twice: unverified
- System prompt resent on every call: unverified
- Guard-model calls billed as separate requests: unverified
- Model deprecations: unverified


### Rate limits and access restrictions


**At 10 requests per minute** , a preview account can't serve more than one request every six seconds, so a customer-facing chat feature queues almost immediately. The 250,000 tokens-per-minute cap matters less unless your prompts are long.


If access sits behind a waitlist, your launch date belongs to Meta, not to you. The bootstrap version: build and test on one small model, and add a queue so bursts wait rather than fail.


### Retries that double Llama API token costs


If your client retries a failed call and Meta bills the failed attempt, you pay twice for one answer. Cap retries at two and log every one, so you can see the cost.


A retry-and-log chain is ten small steps instead of two big ones, and per-step billing charges you for that discipline, so you pay roughly five times as much.


Activepieces, which reaches the API over HTTP, doesn't make you choose: its pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, so the ten-step chain costs what the two-step shortcut did, while Zapier counts every task and Make every module.


Meta's per-token charge still applies to every call the chain makes.


Then there is the system prompt, sent with every request. A 1,000-token prompt across 100,000 calls is 100 million input tokens, and at the 8B input rate of $0.02 per million that costs $2, meaning massive request volumes are affordable. At Maverick's $0.35 it costs $35.


When you add a guard model to screen inputs or outputs, each screened message may be another call carrying its own tokens, so check how Meta meters it.


### Model deprecations and price changes


In late 2026, prices moved in opposite directions. According to ([source](https://www.writeworks.ai/ai-updates/meta) ), Llama 3.1 8B input fell from $0.05 to $0.02 per million tokens, which means **input costs dropped 60%** .


Output fell from $0.08 to $0.04, halving your output costs. Your total bill falls by less than half unless input and output are balanced.


Maverick went the other way: input rose from $0.1875 to $0.35 and output from $0.6525 to $1. Its output price is up about 53%, so a Maverick-based budget set earlier now understates spend by roughly that much on output-heavy work.


Check Meta's page on the day you budget rather than trusting a figure copied here. If a deprecation notice forces a move to a pricier model, you'll want the old numbers on file to measure the jump.
